17 A man has a mass of 80 kg. He ties himself to one end of a rope which passes over a single fixed
pulley. He pulls on the other end of the rope to lift himself up at an average speed of 50 cm s–1.
What is the average useful power at which he is working?
A
40 W
B
0.39 kW
C
4.0 kW
D
39 kW

hints: Notice the lifting speed is $50 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ - convert it to $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ before using it in a power equation.
At constant average speed the pulling force must balance the man's weight $mg$, with $m = 80 \text{ kg}$.
Combine force and speed with $P = Fv = mgv$ and check the result in watts, then in kilowatts.
walkthrough: Identify the useful output: the man's weight is raised at $v = 50 \text{ cm s}^{-1} = 0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
For lifting at constant speed, the useful force equals weight: $F = mg = 80 \times 9.81 \text{ N}$.
Use average useful power $P = Fv = mgv$.
Convert to kilowatts: $392 \text{ W} \approx 0.39 \text{ kW}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $80 \times 0.50 = 40$, so weight $mg$ was replaced by mass $m$. The force to lift at constant speed must be $mg$.

B.explanation: Useful power is $P = Fv = mgv$ with $v = 0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, giving about $392 \text{ W} = 0.39 \text{ kW}$.

C.explanation: About ten times too large, from an error converting $50 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to metres per second, such as using $5.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: About one hundred times too large, from using $v = 50$ in $mgv$ without converting $50 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
